name: Joseph Pierre Jose Adams (Jose2)
notable_stories: Freighted with mule trains up the Arkansas River to Denver in 1863
He was active in moving the Douglas County seat to Castle Rock

In 1863 he took the train to St. Joe and stage to Leavenworth, then hired on as a six-yoke ox-team driver on the Santa Fe trail; at Larned, Kansas Comanches attacked the camp, killed the wagon master and took the oxen, and troops from the Larned post rescued the party the next day.

While in office he helped secure construction of the Castle Rock courthouse (only $14,000 of $20,000 in voted bonds was needed) and was active in moving the county seat from Frenchtown to Castle Rock.

As a boy during the Civil War he left unsettled Missouri in 1863, went to St. Joe and Leavenworth, and hired on as a driver of a six-yoke ox team to Santa Fe. At Larned, Kansas, Comanches attacked the camp, fought all afternoon, killed the wagon master and took the oxen; government troops from the Larned post rescued the party the next day.
He stated that his grandfather died of accidental poisoning, and the grandfather's newly found obituary confirms it.
milestones: Served in the Colorado House of Delegates
Was a member of the Democratic state central committee
Established a stock business in Douglas County before moving to Denver
Crossed the plains by ox cart and settled in Douglas County before Colorado became a state
Died 1923 at the home of his daughter Alice Adams Fulton, 1620 Steele Street, Denver
education: Attended school a few months in Nebraska City, then spent a year on the home farm
Attended school in Nebraska City for a few months, then spent a year on the home farm.
career: Pioneer cattleman on the ranges of Colorado, Wyoming, Arizona and New Mexico
One of the organizers and for many years president of the Denver Livestock Exchange
Helped found what became the National Western Stock Show, with former Governor Ammons and the late Fred Johnson
Douglas County commissioner; a leading spirit in building the courthouse at Castle Rock
Livestock commission business at the Denver stockyards for about 25 years
President of the J. P. Adams & Brigham Livestock Company
Drove a six-mule train up the Arkansas River to Fort Lyons, Pueblo and Denver, first seeing Denver in July 1863
Stage driver for six months from Julesburg to Fort Morgan, then eighteen months freighting
Returned to Colorado in 1869 and started a cattle ranch
Member of the firm Adams & Green at Castle Rock for fourteen years
Commission merchant in Denver; also owned a ranch at Corona on Kiowa Creek, sixty miles east of Denver, raising cattle and horses (1898)
Douglas County commissioner for two three-year terms, re-elected chairman each year
Elected county sheriff in 1875 on the Democratic ticket in a Republican county
Engaged in business in Denver as a commission merchant. (1898)
Owned a ranch at Corona raising cattle and horses. (1898)
Served as Douglas County commissioner for two three-year terms, re-elected chairman each year.
After the Larned encounter, drove a six-mule train up the Arkansas River to Fort Lyons, Pueblo and Denver, first seeing Denver in July 1863.
Worked six months as a stage driver from Julesburg to Fort Morgan, then eighteen months freighting.
For fourteen years a member of the firm of Adams & Green at Castle Rock.
